purpose: Verify Crew Recovery independently from aircraft recovery: delayed WB5_C1 misses F102, so qualified spare WB5_C2 should cover F102/F103 under canonical zero crew-reassignment cost; a high crew-reassignment override should flip the solution back to delay propagation with WB5_C1.

comparison_logic.spare_crew_plan: F101 +60 by C1; F102/F103 on time by C2; F104 on time by C1.
comparison_logic.original_crew_delay_plan: F101 +60, F102 +30, F103 +20, F104 original, all by C1.
comparison_logic.default_reason: Canonical crew_reassignment cost is 0, so the spare-crew plan costs only the forced 60-minute delay.
comparison_logic.high_cost_reason: With crew_reassignment=100, the two reassigned operating legs would add 200 crew cost, so keeping C1 and accepting 50 extra minutes of downstream delay is cheaper.

manual_checks: Visualization shows WB5_F101 as the direct disruption exposure while WB5_AC2 remains available at B for F102/F103.
Default-cost recovery keeps both aircraft on their original rotations and reassigns only crew on F102/F103.
WB5_C2 starts at B, operates B-C-B, and finishes at required terminal B without deadhead.
WB5_C1 operates delayed F101, waits at B, then operates F104 and finishes at required terminal A.
With crew_reassignment=100, F102/F103 delay instead and WB5_C1 retains all four operated legs.
No passenger effects, ferry legs, or cancellations appear in either variant.
design_notes: The case deliberately separates aircraft and crew rotations: WB5_AC1 operates F101/F104 while WB5_AC2 operates F102/F103. This makes F101 delay a crew-connection problem without making the aircraft for F102 unavailable.
Both crews are E1-qualified; rating therefore permits the intended substitution.
No deadhead is required in the intended solution, keeping Case 005 focused on operating-crew reassignment.
aircraft_reassignment is overridden to 100 in both variants to remove canonical zero-cost aircraft-swap degeneracy and keep the test crew-specific.
The high crew-cost variant is secondary to the main Crew Recovery test and provides an additional deterministic decision-flip check.
